correctness.rationale: Every labelled square has exactly four forced stub matches. Conditional on these matches, residual stubs form a uniform matching. The disjoint cases of one forced plus one residual parallel edge, and two residual parallel edges, yield the exact conditional expectation Q. Independent exact rational enumeration of all matchings for the seven listed small models confirms the formula, including the size-four exception. The polynomial sign proof uses the admissibility bound L>=2max(d,e), covers all integer degrees, and the asymptotics follow by direct expansion.

originality.rationale: The checked primary texts concern marginal multiple-edge counts in the pairing model or cycles in simple biregular graphs. None of the inspected relevant results states or implies the all-parameter mixed covariance and its degree-two sign/decay transition. The claim is distinct from superficially similar covariance formulas in other random-graph models. This is a bounded originality judgment, with the literature risks recorded below.
residual_risks: An unindexed historical exact factorial-moment formula for the bipartite pairing model could imply the covariance by specialization; the inspected sources and searches cannot rule out all such literature.
Model distinctions (stub-weighted multigraphs versus uniformly distributed simple or unlabelled multigraphs) must be preserved; transferring the result between them would be incorrect.

value.rationale: Parallel-edge pairs and four-cycles are canonical minimal short-cycle defects in bipartite configuration graphs, used in simplicity and Poisson approximations. The full finite parameter classification contains the unexpected non-monotone degree-two exception and a sign reversal as soon as either degree exceeds two, together with distinct sharp L^-2 and L^-1 covariance regimes. It supplies interpretable joint-dependence information that marginal cycle laws cannot provide.
